en: The Questions of King Milinda, Chapter on the Determination of Formless Phenomena: 13. The Question on the Single Taste of the Ocean "Venerable sir, it is said, 'the great ocean has a single taste, the taste of salt. In what way, venerable sir, does the great ocean have a single taste, the taste of salt? "Just as, great king, the great ocean has but one taste, the taste of salt, even so, great king, this Dhamma and Discipline have but one taste, the taste of liberation. "But, venerable sir, how is it that this Dhamma and Discipline have but one taste, the taste of liberation? "Just as, great king, the great ocean is not filled up by the waters of all the rivers that flow into it, but remains the same, neither increasing nor decreasing; even so, great king, when many bhikkhus attain final Nibbāna by the Nibbāna-element without residue remaining, they do not fill up that Nibbāna-element, which remains the same, neither increasing nor decreasing. It is in this way, great king, that this Dhamma and Discipline have but one taste, the taste of liberation. "But, venerable sir, how is it that this Dhamma and Discipline have but one taste, the taste of liberation? "Just as, great king, the great ocean is not defiled by the corpses of dead men or animals that are cast into it, but remains pure; even so, great king, when many bhikkhus pass away by the final passing away, they do not defile that Nibbāna-element, which remains pure. It is in this way, great king, that this Dhamma and Discipline have but one taste, the taste of liberation. "But, venerable sir, how is it that this Dhamma and Discipline have but one taste, the taste of liberation? "Just as, great king, the great ocean is the abode of such mighty beings as the Timi, the Timingala, the Timitimingala, the Asuras, the Nāgas, and the Gandhabbas; even so, great king, this Dhamma and Discipline is the abode of such mighty beings as the Stream-enterer, the Once-returner, the Non-returner, and the Arahant. It is in this way, great king, that this Dhamma and Discipline have but one taste, the taste of liberation. "But, venerable sir, how is it that this Dhamma and Discipline have but one taste, the taste of liberation? "Just as, great king, the great ocean possesses many wonderful and marvelous qualities; even so, great king, this Dhamma and Discipline possesses many wonderful and marvelous qualities. It is in this way, great king, that this Dhamma and Discipline have but one taste, the taste of liberation. "But, venerable sir, how is it that this Dhamma and Discipline have but one taste, the taste of liberation? "Just as, great king, the great ocean is the source of many precious things, such as pearls, gems, lapis lazuli, conch shells, quartz, coral, silver, gold, rubies, and emeralds; even so, great king, this Dhamma and Discipline is the source of many precious things, such as the fruits of the path and the fruits of the practice. It is in this way, great king, that this Dhamma and Discipline have but one taste, the taste of liberation. "But, venerable sir, how is it that this Dhamma and Discipline have but one taste, the taste of liberation? "Just as, great king, the great ocean is the abode of the Four Great Kings, of Sakka the lord of devas, of Brahmā Sahampati, and of other powerful devas; even so, great king, this Dhamma and Discipline is the abode of the Four Noble Ones, of the Stream-enterer, the Once-returner, the Non-returner, and the Arahant. It is in this way, great king, that this Dhamma and Discipline have but one taste, the taste of liberation. "But, venerable sir, how is it that this Dhamma and Discipline have but one taste, the taste of liberation? "Just as, great king, the great ocean is the place where the sun and moon rise and set, illuminating the world with their radiance;

even so, great king, this Dhamma and Discipline is the place where the Buddhas arise, illuminating the world with the radiance of their wisdom. It is in this way, great king, that this Dhamma and Discipline have but one taste, the taste of liberation. "But, venerable sir, how is it that this Dhamma and Discipline have but one taste, the taste of liberation? "Just as, great king, the great ocean is the limit of the earth, and beyond it lies the land of Jambudīpa; even so, great king, this Dhamma and Discipline is the limit of the holy life, and beyond it there is no higher state. It is in this way, great king, that this Dhamma and Discipline have but one taste, the taste of liberation. "It is wonderful, venerable sir! It is marvelous, venerable sir! How well this has been stated by the Blessed One: 'Just as the great ocean has but one taste, the taste of salt, even so this Dhamma and Discipline has but one taste, the taste of liberation. "It is because of these nine reasons, great king, that this Dhamma and Discipline has but one taste, the taste of liberation. "Excellent, venerable sir! Excellent, venerable sir! Just as one might set upright what had been overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or show the way to one who was lost, or bring an oil lamp into a dark place so that those with eyes might see forms, even so has the Blessed One made the Dhamma clear in many ways. I go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dhamma, and to the Sangha of Bhikkhus. May the Blessed One accept me as a lay follower who has taken refuge from this day forth for as long as life shall last."
"Venerable Nāgasena, for what reason is the ocean of one taste, the taste of salt?
"Because the water has remained there for a long time, Great King, the ocean is of one taste, the taste of salt."
This is the thirteenth problem, on the single taste of the ocean.
